A question of structure versus flexibility, this is. SQL databases -- like PostgreSQL or MySQL -- rigid tables with defined schemas they use, and strong at enforcing relationships between data they are. NoSQL databases -- such as MongoDB or DynamoDB -- schema-flexible they are, storing documents or key-value pairs, and scale horizontally with ease they do. If well-defined relationships your data has, SQL you should choose; if varied and fast-changing the shape of your data is, serve you well NoSQL may.
